rules.subject: x0r0_bypass
rules.message: a block on this seam is far worse conditioned than the operator it assembles into, and every diagnostic downstream of L4 is taken on the sum: F10 kappa 1254 against the assembled 1.09 (1150x). The assembled numbers are not wrong and they are not sufficient: beta_i is what the substructuring branch inverts (W57) and Xi_i is the composability index, and neither is recoverable from the sum. The mechanism here is one-sidedness -- block norms F00 0.2154, F10 0.06657, assembled 0.234 Per-mode, read off alpha_star, the dominant side holds median 0.975 and max 1.000 of the response, with 25 of 25 modes above 0.90. Substitution of the weak side is invisible below beta_min = 0.1481 for F10.

rules.subject: R1_down
rules.message: passivity defect 1.807e+00 on the assembled seam: the symmetric part has a negative mode, so the L <= 1 branch is unavailable and L falls back to fitted. The eigenvector names which interface mode is amplified. **W306: the spectrum is ONE-SIGNED NEGATIVE** (lambda_max = -1.776e+00 < 0), so every mode is damped and this is a global SIGN rather than an amplified mode -- S lam = chi is indifferent to it because chi flips with S. That makes it a DECLARATION inconsistency rather than a physical defect: the seam declares no effort_normal, so both blocks entered the sum with +1. The L <= 1 branch is still unavailable until the orientation is fixed, which is why this is still a decertification

scheme Sigma
  D_decomposition        overlapping   <- as declared
  D_decomposition_axes   ['overlapping']
  Lambda_transmission    dirichlet   <- probing is the exception that makes R1 survivable: probed-DtN requires only bc_channel >= dirichlet, because the higher rung is built outside the expert
  O_ordering             additive   <- multiplicative ordering is forbidden when any composition-layer guarantee depends on equivalent treatment of agents; a direct Schur solve satisfies this automatically, being order-free
  K_accelerator          direct-schur   <- a direct Schur solve makes the solve-incompleteness term vanish, and is order-free so it satisfies R5 by construction rather than by discipline
  C_levels               one   <- one level; a classical coarse solve would require an agent that can run at a different window size without changing its regime
  W_window               1 (DEFAULTED)   <- W* would be about 1/ln(L) clamped by R3, and L is unmeasured (W1), so W* is UNCOMPUTABLE. W = 1 is the honest default and this is the compiler saying it is defaulting rather than choosing
  eps_tol                None (DEFAULTED)   <- unset: the relative rule needs measured tau and sigma (W3)
  overlap                0.5
  exchange_interval      0.2   <- the exchange interval cannot go below max_i dt_native. The window is the one axis a frozen expert can move along: W can be increased, never decreased
  multirate              False
  flux_matching          single-clock
